title: Routing Networks with logical Mirror blocks
hypothesis: A shared canonical nonlinear block plus two continuous Mirror coordinates recovers held-out task functions more accurately than a finite prototype-block Routing Network while using no more N=20 bytes than independent per-task blocks.
physical_object: one canonical tanh function block with fixed deterministic activation
mirror_coordinate: continuous input scale and shift (a,b) applied before the shared block
logical_multiplicity: continuous logical function blocks from one physical canonical block
controls: Routing Networks with K=4 prototype blocks
Routing Networks with K=8 prototype blocks
one shared block with no Mirror coordinates
shared block plus two Mirror coordinates
success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror quality beats selected Routing Network by >=10% and N=20 actual bytes are <= independent full per-task blocks; report the Pareto comparison with K=4 and K=8.
failure_gate: Routing Network matches Mirror at equal/fewer bytes, Mirror has no quality gain over independent blocks, or any per-world quality/byte gate misses.
boundaries: Scalar nonlinear regression mechanism screen only.
The activation block is deterministic and shared; scale/shift inputs are paid task codes.
No large-network or natural task claim.
